title: Stabilize crypto native bindings and refresh SSO dependencies across services
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated several ad-hoc fixes to support different OpenSSL/JWT/SAML client implementations across our services. Recent incidents (rotation failures and a staging regression when the base image moved to OpenSSL 3) revealed brittle native bindings (Go cgo consumers, Python wheels with OpenSSL linkage, and one Node native addon used by legacy auth-worker). Goal: perform a coordinated, low-risk upgrade and remediation across affected services so we have a stable, reproducible crypto surface and modern SSO libraries with predictable behaviour across platforms. This ticket coordinates the cross-service plan, acceptance criteria, and rollout path.
sub_tasks: Inventory: produce a per-service matrix of OpenSSL usage, linked native bindings, and SSO/JWT packages (Go stdlib wrappers, node-jsonwebtoken, passport-saml, python-saml).
Introduce lightweight crypto-abstraction shim in auth-common for platform-agnostic callers (pure-Go wrappers + optional native fallback).
Upgrade OpenSSL in official base images to 3.1.x and publish hermetic images for canary clusters.
Rebuild and publish Python wheels for auth-sdk and saml-util pinned to OpenSSL 3 ABI-compatible builds; verify manylinux tags.
Replace deprecated passport-saml consumer in identity-web with maintained fork and update SAML assertion parsing to tolerate attribute order changes.
Bump jwt libraries where necessary (node-jsonwebtoken -> 9.x, java-> nimbus-jose-jwt 10.x) and update token validation tests.
Create migration PRs for three critical services (auth-api, identity-web, auth-worker) with feature flags and canary deploys.
End-to-end regression test run using recorded SAML flows and replay harness; prepare rollback path.
Security review and package audit before production rollout.
acceptance_criteria: All services in inventory successfully build against OpenSSL 3 images without linker/runtime errors in staging.
SAML login success rate in staging >= 99.9% during a 48h soak with real auth sample traffic.
No increase in average auth latency > 15% compared to baseline after upgrades (measured by auth-api traces).
New auth-common shim has API compatibility tests covering token validation, signing, and KV cache interaction and is adopted by at least auth-api and identity-web.
Security team signs off on dependency SBOM and vulnerability scan results (no critical CVEs outstanding or mitigations documented).
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Rodriguez: Created ticket after post-mortem highlighted OpenSSL ABI fragility; initial inventory kickoff.
2026-02-25 Liam Chen: Finished initial inventory matrix and surfaced three high-risk consumers: auth-worker native addon, python auth-sdk wheels, and identity-web passport-saml usage.
2026-03-03 Design review (Slack): Decided on adding a minimal crypto-abstraction in auth-common rather than a full refactor to speed rollout.
2026-03-10 QA: Rebuilt python wheels and validated manylinux2014 wheel links on staging nodes; one wheel failed due to missing openssl dev headers in build image — fixed in base image PR.
2026-03-12 Liam Chen: Started canary deploy of identity-web on staging with feature flag 'openssl3-sso' enabled for 5% of traffic.
risks: ABI mismatch causes runtime crashes in low-volume languages (Python/Node native addons).
SAML assertion parsing differences lead to failed logins for customers using older IdPs.
Token validation differences could cause subtle acceptance regressions (clock skew and alg mismatches).
Build pipeline changes could delay other releases if base images are promoted incorrectly.
rollback_plan: Each service change behind a feature flag. If canary shows auth error rate > 0.1% above baseline or latency spike > 15% for 30m, flip flag off and roll back image tag. For package-heavy changes (python wheels), revert to previous pinned wheel in package registry and redeploy staging/prod nodes using the pinned artifact.
test_plan: Unit tests for crypto-abstraction with recorded vectors for RSA/EC signing and verification.
Integration: run SAML replay harness (saml-replay infra) against identity-web staging deployment.
E2E: run nightly production-like soak in canary region for 48h with traffic mirror of 2% and assert metrics (login success, latency).
Automated vulnerability scan of built images and SBOM diff; block on any new critical vulnerabilities.
